requirements.title: A RETURN statement has RETURN and an optional scalar integer expression
requirements.definition: The RETURN statement syntax is RETURN followed optionally by a scalar integer expression.

requirements.title: RETURN appears inside a function or subroutine inclusive scope
requirements.definition: A RETURN statement appears in the inclusive scope of a function or subroutine subprogram.

requirements.title: RETURN alternate-return expression selects the nth alternate branch target
requirements.definition: For RETURN with expression value n in range 1 through the number of asterisks, the invoking CALL branches to the nth alternate return specifier target.

pending.return-selects-first-alternate: Subroutine s(*,*) executes RETURN 1; caller initializes token=-9, CALL s(*100,*200), label 100 sets token=101, label 200 sets 202, and expected token is exact 101.
pending.return-selects-second-alternate: Same source shape with RETURN 2 expects exact token 202, proving index selection rather than any alternate branch.

requirements.title: RETURN without an in-range alternate value performs no alternate transfer
requirements.definition: RETURN with no expression, or with an expression outside the valid alternate-return range, performs no transfer of control to an alternate return.

requirements.title: END statements execute as RETURN without an expression
requirements.definition: Execution of an end-function-stmt, end-mp-subprogram-stmt, or end-subroutine-stmt is equivalent to execution of RETURN without an expression.

pending.end-subroutine-normal-return: Subroutine reaches END SUBROUTINE after assigning x=41; caller observes exact 41 and no alternate branch.
pending.end-function-normal-return: Integer function reaches END FUNCTION after result=42; caller observes exact 42.
pending.end-module-procedure-normal-return: Module subroutine reaches END SUBROUTINE after assigning x=43; caller USEs the module and observes exact 43.
pending.end-mp-subprogram-normal-return: Separate module procedure plan: ancestor module declares MODULE SUBROUTINE fill(x) with INTEGER, INTENT(OUT) :: x; submodule body MODULE PROCEDURE fill assigns x=44 and reaches END PROCEDURE. Caller initializes x=-44 and token=-99, CALL fill(x), then the next Fortran statement sets token=99; expect x==44 and token==99.

review_rationale: Source registration for 15.6.2.6 (ENTRY), 15.6.2.7 (RETURN), 15.6.2.8 (CONTAINS), 15.6.3 (procedures defined by means other than Fortran) and 15.6.4 (statement functions) (batch236). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across three rounds; R1544-R1547 and C1579-C1591 had no existing tests and carry conforming one-feature controls, and non-Fortran procedures are observed through mixed Fortran/C builds. Source accounting only; completes Clause 15.
